description: Iranian nomadic confederation (c. 1st–15th c.) originating in the steppe north of the Caucasus; Hunnic pressure drove Alan groups westward into Europe during the Migration Period, some reaching Iberia and North Africa, while eastern Alans in the Caucasus established the Alania kingdom that adopted Orthodox Christianity; the Alans' descendants are the modern Ossetians of the central Caucasus.

temporal.notes: Stub: dates from GeoJSON basemap years 700–1100

lifecycle_phases.description: Iranian-speaking Alans dominated the steppes north of the Caucasus and Caspian, raiding into Persia and the Roman East.
Hunnic invasion shattered Alan unity; remnant groups migrated westward with Gothic federations into Gaul and Spain.
Alan fragments established short-lived settlements in Gaul and north Africa before being absorbed by Visigoths and Vandals.
Alans in the Caucasus (ancestors of modern Ossetians) maintained independence under Khazar and later Byzantine overlordship.

rise_factors.description: Alan heavy cavalry tactics made them feared mercenaries and raiders across late antiquity.
Command of the Pontic steppe gave access to vast pastures and rapid strategic mobility.

decline_factors.description: Mongol invasions of 1222-1239 devastated the Caucasian Alans and ended their political independence.
Diaspora groups in western Europe were rapidly assimilated into dominant host cultures.
